import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a figure with subplots for comprehensive insights
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# 1. Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :2])
sensor_colors = {'Full Frame': '#e74c3c', 'APS-C': '#3498db', 'Micro 4/3': '#2ecc71', 'Medium Format': '#f39c12'}
for sensor in df['sensor_type'].unique():
    sensor_data = df[df['sensor_type'] == sensor]
    ax1.scatter(sensor_data['megapixels'], sensor_data['price_usd'], 
               alpha=0.6, s=50, label=sensor, color=sensor_colors.get(sensor, '#95a5a6'))
ax1.set_xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_title('Camera Price vs Megapixels by Sensor Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
ax1.legend(title='Sensor Type', frameon=True, shadow=True)
ax1.grid(alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# 2. Brand Distribution
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
brand_counts = df['brand'].value_counts().head(8)
colors_palette = sns.color_palette('Set2', len(brand_counts))
ax2.barh(brand_counts.index, brand_counts.values, color=colors_palette)
ax2.set_xlabel('Count', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_title('Top 8 Camera Brands', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax2.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# 3. Price Distribution by Body Type
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :2])
body_types = df['body_type'].unique()
price_data = [df[df['body_type'] == bt]['price_usd'].dropna() for bt in body_types]
bp = ax3.boxplot(price_data, labels=body_types, patch_artist=True, showfliers=False)
for patch, color in zip(bp['boxes'], sns.color_palette('husl', len(body_types))):
    patch.set_facecolor(color)
    patch.set_alpha(0.7)
ax3.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Body Type', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax3.set_title('Price Distribution by Body Type', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
ax3.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# 4. 4K Video Capability Distribution
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
video_4k_counts = df['has_video_4k'].value_counts()
labels = ['No 4K', '4K']
colors_4k = ['#e74c3c', '#27ae60']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax4.pie(video_4k_counts.values, labels=labels, autopct='%1.1f%%',
                                     colors=colors_4k, startangle=90, textprops={'fontsize': 10, 'weight': 'bold'})
ax4.set_title('4K Video Capability', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)

# 5. Weight vs Price colored by 4K capability
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, :2])
df_4k = df[df['has_video_4k'] == 1]
df_no4k = df[df['has_video_4k'] == 0]
ax5.scatter(df_no4k['weight_grams'], df_no4k['price_usd'], alpha=0.5, s=40, c='#e74c3c', label='No 4K')
ax5.scatter(df_4k['weight_grams'], df_4k['price_usd'], alpha=0.5, s=40, c='#27ae60', label='Has 4K')
ax5.set_xlabel('Weight (grams)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=11, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_title('Camera Weight vs Price (4K Capability)', fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', pad=15)
ax5.legend(frameon=True, shadow=True)
ax5.grid(alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# 6. Max ISO by Sensor Type
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 2])
sensor_iso = df.groupby('sensor_type')['max_iso'].mean().sort_values(ascending=True)
colors_iso = sns.color_palette('coolwarm', len(sensor_iso))
ax6.barh(sensor_iso.index, sensor_iso.values, color=colors_iso)
ax6.set_xlabel('Avg Max ISO', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_title('Avg Max ISO by Sensor', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', pad=10)
ax6.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# Overall title
fig.suptitle('Digital Camera Market Analysis Dashboard', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.995)

plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
